investigation: when does CAGRA outperform brute_force for Layer 2/3 anomaly-distance search
original_hypothesis_from_pitch: CAGRA is designed for huge graphs and will win as the historical attractor map scales to 10k-100k+ points in production
finding: hypothesis was WRONG as originally stated; index size alone does not determine the crossover, query batch size does

single_query_scale_sweep.note: brute_force vs CAGRA at query_batch_size=1, varying index size from 300 to 500,000 points
single_query_scale_sweep.result: brute_force wins at every tested index size (300 to 500,000 points); CAGRA never wins at batch_size=1

cpu_comparison_at_500k_points_batch_1.note: CPU and GPU are within the same order of magnitude at batch_size=1 against a 500k-point index; neither dominates decisively, unlike Layer 1 where CPU/AVX2 won by 2.7-26x

revised_architectural_recommendation: the crossover for CAGRA is query BATCH SIZE (roughly 1000+), not index size; CAGRA does not help the single-tick hot path regardless of how large the historical attractor map grows

for tick-by-tick (batch_size=1) anomaly-distance search, CPU (ball_tree) and GPU (brute_force) perform comparably (within ~20% of each other) even against a 500,000-point index; this needs re-testing on the actual target deployment hardware before committing to either
CAGRA should be used only for batch/windowed workloads: periodic Section 4.4 background re-clustering, or bulk re-scoring of historical windows, not the live single-tick decision path

this directly revises the previously proposed heterogeneous architecture: Layer 2/3 anomaly search does NOT need to run on GPU/CAGRA for the hot path; it can run on CPU or GPU-brute-force interchangeably at batch_size=1, and GPU/CAGRA is reserved specifically for the async refit workload where it was already planned to run
